about: The contract of the extension run. Every check id lives here and nowhere else is the list kept.
The extension (tests/extension), the test pages (tests/extension/pages), the page server, the run script and the report all follow it.
The dry run (scripts/extension-test.sh --dry-run) fails on any id used in the code that is not listed here, and on any listed id that no code records.

results.works: The call returned and the value was what the check expects. A call that returns but with the wrong value is fails.
results.fails: The call returned an error, threw, timed out, or returned a wrong value. detail carries the error text or the value's shape.
results.crashes: The browser process ended while this check was in flight (its begin marker was sent, its result never came). Assigned by the report, never by the extension.
results.absent: The API or event is undefined in that context.
results.not-run: The check could not be attempted, and detail says why (for example: no tab to act on, or risky checks switched off).
results.no-record: Assigned by the report: nothing arrived for this id on any path. Never counted as works.

record.id: a check id from this file, or a control id
record.group: the check's group from this file
record.result: works | fails | crashes | absent | not-run (begin markers have none)
record.detail: string or small JSON value: error text, or the shape of the returned value
record.by: worker | content | page | popup | options | script
record.launch: launch number, from config.js (extension) or the server's launch file (pages)
record.boot: worker records only: the boot id of the worker instance that sent it
record.phase: "begin" on the marker a worker check sends before its call; absent on results
record.final: false on a provisional result (an event not fired by the end of the suite); a later final result for the same id replaces it
record.added by the server: via: "http", received: server time in ms

config_js.about: config.js in the extension folder. The repository holds a placeholder with server null. The run script writes the real one into its own copy of the extension before each launch.
config_js.shape: self.ASS_TEST = {server: 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>', xserver: 'http://localhost:<port>', extensionId: '<id>', launch: <n>, risky: true|false, skip: ['<check id>', ...]};

endpoints.GET /<file>: a file from tests/extension/pages. /start.html also sets the cookie ass_server_cookie=1; Path=/; SameSite=Lax
endpoints.POST /__ass/record: body: one record or an array of records, as JSON sent with Content-Type text/plain. Appended to records.jsonl. Answers 204 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
endpoints.OPTIONS /__ass/*: 204 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type
endpoints.GET /__ass/has?id=<id>: {"has": true|false}: whether a result record (not a begin marker) with that id has arrived in the current launch
endpoints.GET /__ass/count?id=<id>: {"count": <n>}: how many result records with that id have arrived in the current launch (tabs.reload uses it to see a second ctl.page.ready)
endpoints.POST /__ass/login: body JSON {user, pass}. Appended to logins.jsonl. Answers {"ok": true, "user": "<user>"}
endpoints.GET /__dnr/static-block.txt: body: not-blocked (a static rule must stop this request before it reaches the server)
endpoints.GET /__dnr/static-block.js: body: window.assStaticScriptRan = true; (a static rule must stop it)
endpoints.GET /__dnr/static-redirect-src.txt: body: not-redirected (a static rule must redirect it to /__dnr/redirect-target.txt)
endpoints.GET /__dnr/dynamic-block.txt: body: not-blocked (the dynamic rule added at run time must stop it)
endpoints.every request: one line in requests.jsonl: {t, launch, method, path (without query), host, cookies: [cookie names]}

run_dir_files.server.port: the port the page server bound on 127.0.0.1
run_dir_files.launch: the current launch number, written by the run script before each launch, read by the server
run_dir_files.cdp-records.jsonl: records read through the debug port (path 2)
run_dir_files.script.jsonl: records written by the run script itself (by: script)
run_dir_files.requests.jsonl: every request the page server received
run_dir_files.launches.jsonl: one line per launch: {launch, pid, profile, started, ended, exit, signal, quit_requested, ended_before_quit, quit_seconds, helpers_left, tmp_left}
run_dir_files.plan-<n>.json: the ids skipped in launch n: only the checks that crashed the browser in an earlier launch. Everything else runs again, because page checks depend on what the worker sets up in the same launch
run_dir_files.app-<n>.log: the app's own output in launch n

control.what: Posted at the top of every worker start. detail {bootId, wake}: wake is true when the suite of this launch was already done (a restart after idle).
The worker suite starts. detail {testTabId, foundBy}.
The worker suite has ended and the wake alarm is set.
Tabs and windows the suite created, and whether removing them worked.
boot.html saw the worker (or gave up waiting) and is moving to start.html. detail {waitedMs, sawWorker}.
start.html has made all its declarativeNetRequest requests.
victim.html loaded in the popup the run script opened.
created-tab.html loaded (tabs.create made a real tab).
created-window.html loaded (windows.create made a real window).
nav.html loaded (after tabs.update with a url).
nav2.html loaded (the run script's navigation that wakes an idle worker).
popup.html has recorded all its checks.
options.html has recorded all its checks.

checks.what: After quit, the profile's Secure Preferences lists the extension id with location 8 (kCommandLine, '--load-extension', extensions/common/mojom/manifest.mojom at 156.0.8078.100).
A service_worker target at chrome-extension://<id>/ appears on the debug port within 30 s of launch.
cs_start.js ran in start.html's main frame while document.readyState was 'loading'.
cs_start.js ran in frame.html from 127.0.0.1 inside start.html.
cs_start.js ran in frame.html from localhost inside start.html (another site, so another renderer process).
cs_idle.js ran in start.html's main frame with document.readyState 'interactive' or 'complete'.
cs_idle.js ran in the 127.0.0.1 frame.
cs_idle.js ran in the localhost frame.
The content script sees the page's DOM (data-ass-page='start') but not the page's global window.assPageSecret.
The service worker's script ran in this launch (first boot).
During its first boot the worker handled at least one event the browser dispatched (runtime.onInstalled, runtime.onMessage, a webNavigation event). detail lists which.
After ctl.suite.done, with no debug session on the worker and no open port, its service_worker target leaves the debug port's list within 45 s (Chrome's documented idle limit is 30 s).
A new worker instance (new boot id, wake true) handled an event after the suite was done. detail {wokenBy, bootId, secondsAfterSuiteDone}.
Content script sends {type:'hello'} with runtime.sendMessage; the worker answers {type:'hello-ack'} with the sender's tab id.
Content script opens a port named 'ass-port', sends 3 messages, gets 3 echoes back, then disconnects.
Worker sends {type:'worker-ping'} to the test tab with tabs.sendMessage; the main frame's content script answers {type:'cs-pong'}.
The 'hello' message's sender carries tab.id, tab.url on start.html and frameId 0.
storage.local.set then get returns the same value. Also leaves fromWorker='set-by-worker' for the popup.
storage.onChanged fired with areaName 'local' for the key just set, within 3 s.
The main frame's content script sets and gets a storage.local key (exposed to content scripts by default, per Chrome's storage docs).
storage.session.set then get returns the same value (worker only: not exposed to content scripts by default, per Chrome's storage docs).
storage.onChanged fired with areaName 'session' for the key just set, within 3 s.
declarativeNetRequest.getEnabledRulesets includes 'static_rules'.
fetch('/__dnr/static-block.txt') from start.html rejects, and the server never received it.
<script src='/__dnr/static-block.js'> fires error and never runs, and the server never received it.
fetch('/__dnr/static-redirect-src.txt') returns 'redirect-target'; the server received the target and never the source.
updateDynamicRules adds rule 100 (block /__dnr/dynamic-block.txt) and getDynamicRules lists it.
After dnr.dynamic.add, fetch('/__dnr/dynamic-block.txt') rejects, and the server never received it.
fetch('/__dnr/control.txt') returns 'control', and the server received it: blocking is specific, not everything.
After ctl.page.dnr_done, getMatchedRules({tabId}) lists rule 1 of 'static_rules' and dynamic rule 100 (needs declarativeNetRequestFeedback, per Chrome's declarativeNetRequest docs).
Event: onRuleMatchedDebug fired for a request from start.html (unpacked extensions with declarativeNetRequestFeedback only, per the same docs).
executeScript({target:{tabId}, func}) into the test tab returns start.html's document.title.
executeScript with world 'MAIN' returns the page global window.assPageSecret.
insertCSS sets #css-target width to 123px; a following executeScript reads the computed width '123px'.
registerContentScripts registers registered.js for http://127.0.0.1/nav*; getRegisteredContentScripts lists it.
registered.js ran when nav.html or nav2.html loaded.
tabs.query({}) returns a list that includes the test tab.
tabs.query({active:true}) returns at least one tab.
tabs.query({active:true, lastFocusedWindow:true}) returns exactly one tab (the usual call of a popup or a password manager).
tabs.query({url:'http://127.0.0.1/start.html*'}) returns the test tab.
tabs.get(testTabId) returns a tab whose url is start.html. detail includes windowId and index.
tabs.getCurrent() in the worker resolves to undefined (Chrome's tabs docs: undefined from a non-tab context).
tabs.getCurrent() in popup.html, loaded in the content view, returns a tab whose url is popup.html.
tabs.update(testTabId, {muted:true}) then tabs.get shows mutedInfo.muted true; then set back to false.
tabs.update(testTabId, {active:true}) resolves with a tab whose active is true.
tabs.captureVisibleTab() resolves to a data:image URL (needs <all_urls> or activeTab, per Chrome's tabs docs). detail: length.
tabs.create({url: created-tab.html, active:false}) resolves with a tab, and ctl.created_tab.loaded arrives within 10 s.
tabs.duplicate(victimTabId) resolves with a new tab id.
tabs.move(victimTabId, {index:0}) resolves with the tab at index 0.
tabs.group({tabIds:[victimTabId]}) resolves with a group id. absent if tabs.group is undefined.
tabs.remove(victimTabId) resolves, and tabs.get(victimTabId) then rejects. Never called on the test tab.
tabs.reload(testTabId) resolves, and ctl.page.ready arrives again within 10 s.
tabs.update(testTabId, {url: nav.html}) resolves, and ctl.nav.loaded arrives within 10 s.
Event fired for any tab (expected after tabs.create or the victim popup).
Event fired for the test tab (expected after tabs.update or tabs.reload).
Event fired for any tab.
Event fired for any tab (expected after tabs.remove).
windows.getAll({populate:true}) returns at least one window containing the test tab.
windows.getCurrent() resolves with a window.
windows.getLastFocused() resolves with a window.
windows.get(id) resolves with that window. id: the test tab's windowId if tabs.get gave one >= 0, else windows.WINDOW_ID_CURRENT (detail says which).
windows.create({url: created-window.html, focused:false}) resolves with a window, and ctl.created_window.loaded arrives within 10 s.
windows.update on the created window ({width:640, height:480}), or else on the test tab's window ({state:'normal'}), resolves.
windows.remove on the window windows.create made resolves. Never called on the test window; not-run when nothing was created.
Event fired for any window.
Event fired for any window.
Event fired.
Event fired.
setBadgeText({text:'ok'}) then getBadgeText({}) returns 'ok'.
setIcon({imageData}) with a 16x16 ImageData drawn on an OffscreenCanvas resolves.
setPopup({popup:'popup.html'}) then getPopup({}) returns a URL ending in /popup.html.
action.openPopup() resolves (Chrome 127+, per Chrome's action docs).
Listener registration only. fails if addListener throws; otherwise not-run, because firing it needs a click on a toolbar button and the app has none.
chrome-extension://<id>/popup.html, loaded in the content view through the debug port, ran its script.
In popup.html: chrome.runtime.id equals the extension id, and chrome.storage.local, chrome.tabs and chrome.action are objects.
In popup.html: storage.local.get('fromWorker') returns 'set-by-worker'.
In popup.html: runtime.sendMessage({type:'popup-ping'}) gets {type:'popup-pong'} from the worker.
chrome-extension://<id>/options.html, loaded in the content view through the debug port, ran its script.
In options.html: chrome.runtime.id equals the extension id, and chrome.storage.local is an object.
Event fired for a URL on the page server.
Event fired for a URL on the page server.
Event fired for a URL on the page server.
Event fired for a URL on the page server.
getAllFrames({tabId: testTabId}) returns 3 frames: start.html and its two frame.html frames.
alarms.create('ass-check', {delayInMinutes: 0.5}) then alarms.get('ass-check') returns it.
Event fired for 'ass-check'.
contextMenus.create({id:'ass-menu', title, contexts:['page']}) gives no runtime.lastError.
permissions.contains({permissions:['tabs'], origins:['http://127.0.0.1/*']}) resolves true.
cookies.get({url: server, name:'ass_server_cookie'}) returns value '1' (set by the server on start.html).
cookies.set({url: server, name:'ass_ext_cookie', value:'set-by-extension'}) then cookies.get returns that value. The report adds whether a later request to the server carried it.
commands.getAll() lists 'ass-test-command' with a non-empty shortcut. Listed with an empty shortcut is fails ('declared, no shortcut registered').
chrome.runtime.id equals config.extensionId (the id the manifest key fixes).
getManifest() returns manifest_version 3 and the test extension's name.
Event fired with reason 'install'.
runtime.openOptionsPage() resolves.

The content script finds #login-user and #login-pass in start.html, sets their values and dispatches input and change events; the page's own input listener reports the same user name (data-ass-seen-user).
The content script calls requestSubmit(); the page posts the values to /__ass/login and marks data-ass-submitted='ok:<user>'.
The same fill in the localhost frame's form; that frame's own listener reports the user name.
Per launch: the browser process was still running when the run script asked it to quit.
Per launch: quit through AppKit by PID exits 0 within 30 s with no helper process left.
